channel.title: Palm Coast Observer - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Palm Coast Observer (observerlocalnews.com)

item.title: Flagler’s settlement offer to Hammock Harbour would allow the 240-unit dry boat storage
item.description: The offer allows Hammock Harbour to develop the site plan as-is. The county would also pay the developer $400,000 in settlement plus $150,000 in impact and building fee credits.

item.title: Sean Adrian Salvacion of Imagine School at Town Center wins Flagler County Spelling Bee
item.description: The seventh grader correctly spelled "silhouette" in the second round and "welterweight" in the 11th round to win the championship and move on to the regional Spelling Bee.

item.title: ICI Homes asks Palm Coast council for more houses in development, Palm Coast Council asks where is the public benefit?
item.description: The council approved the first reading of the application 3-2, but on the condition the developer makes some changes before the second reading.

item.title: Hammock Community Association recommits to preserving The Hammock with new strategic plan
item.description: 'We really thought a lot about the future,' HCA President Stillman said. 'It's hard. You don't have that crystal ball.'

item.title: Volusia County Council to consider placing a 'toilet to tap' ban on 2026 ballot
item.description: The council directed staff on Tuesday, Feb. 3, to draft a charter amendment and county ordinance for consideration at a future meeting.

item.title: 'These are not storage facilities': Ormond commissioners give final OK to new commerce park
item.description: At the Feb. 3 meeting, the commission unanimously approved a development order on second reading for Tomoka Commerce Park at 890 N. U.S. 1.

item.title: Federal judge favors developers in preliminary arguments over development of Tomoka Oaks golf course
item.description: A judge stated in an order that 'it "logically makes sense" to hold governments accountable for uncodified policies that may be applied arbitrarily and capriciously.'

item.title: Eleven-year-old Indian Trails Middle School student arrested for writing school shooting threat on bathroom wall
item.description: The student said she was dared to write the message on the wall.

item.title: The Observer — in your mailbox?
item.description: New 'delivery sponsorships' represent a significant shift in the Observer's distribution.

item.title: Volusia County School Board member Jamie Haynes earns distinction
item.description: Haynes was recognized with the Advanced Certified Board Member by Florida School Boards Association.
